subject: Post-call: GPU silo sizing & isolation options
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Tang <alyssa.tang@orpheus.ai>, Nate Rosenthal <nate.rosenthal@orpheus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: GPU silo sizing & isolation options

Hi Alyssa / Nate —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same view and we can lock next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

What we heard (pain points):
- Noisy neighbors on shared endpoints causing 3x tail latency spikes during batch analytics windows.
- Regulatory requirement: certain models and telemetry must remain within the US and be logically isolated per team.
- Bursty inference pattern: nightly batch re-ranking + daytime interactive requests (peak ~40 rps).
- Concern about cold-start token latency for larger models (70B-ish) at 2k context lengths.

Goals you stated:
- Single-tenant isolation for production models for two internal lines of business (AI Ops & Customer Gen).
- Baseline throughput to sustain 40 rps with headroom for 2–3x burst.
- Target latency: P95 <= 150ms for typical prompts, P99 target < 200ms if possible.
- SOC2 evidence and short turnaround for security questionnaire items.

Our initial sizing notes (ballpark):
- Suggest a dedicated GPU silo: equivalent of 8 x A100-class GPUs (4 baseline reserved, 4 burst-able).
- Prefer instance flavor with NVLink for KV-cache sharing; runtime will use prefix KV caching to reduce token generation cost.
- Options: Dedicated (reserved) pool with tenant isolation + VPC peering, or Private deployment inside your VPC for full network isolation.

Commercial / SLA thoughts (preliminary):
- We can offer monthly reserved commit on 4 GPUs with an agreed burst policy for the additional 4 (buffered capacity).
- SLA targets we expect to meet with the above config: 99.9% uptime, P95 latency SLO monitored in Console, regression alerts tied to your eval prompts.

Attachments: I attached a quick workbook with traffic shape and a crate-level sizing sanity-check (gpu-scaling-sanity-check.xlsx).

Next steps (I propose):
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/SRE + our solutions engineers (Dylan) to validate network and KV-cache requirements (aim: week of 11/23).
2) Security checklist: you to send SOC2 ask/POC items (you mentioned a short questionnaire) — we can return answers and evidence within 3 business days once received.
3) Commercial: Marissa will follow with a draft term sheet and pricing for the 4+4 commit model.

Marissa / Dylan / Vivek — tagging you for ownership: Dylan to schedule the deep-dive, Marissa to lead pricing, Vivek to confirm isolation options and operational runbook.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the sheet together.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: gpu-scaling-sanity-check.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Alyssa Tang <alyssa.tang@orpheus.ai>

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: GPU silo sizing & isolation options

Thanks Hannah — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- The two LOBs must have cryptographic separation of model artifacts and telemetry; per-team keys (KMS) are preferred.
- For the SOC2 items: we have a short list (data retention, access logs, key rotation). I'll attach the questionnaire now.
- On latency: the P99 <200ms is a hard goal for interactive flows — we understand it may be model-dependent; can you call out any trade-offs?

We attached the SOC/ops ask as "orpheus-soc2-ask-20261115.pdf". Can you confirm a rough timeline for providing the answers and any supporting artifacts?

Also — on the proposal structure, we'd prefer a baseline reserved commit for predictable billing and then a defined burst pool with clear billing rules.

Looking forward to the deep-dive — available Tuesday or Thursday afternoons PT next week.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Orpheus follow-up & owner tasks (internal)

Internal note — please treat as internal-only for coordination. Short plan and owner assignments based on Alyssa's reply.

Summary of external asks:
- KMS per-team keying + evidence for key rotation and access controls.
- SOC2-specific artifacts: data retention policy, audit log extracts, staff access matrix.
- Firm P99 latency target (they asked P99 <200ms for interactive).
- Commercial: baseline reserved commit + burst pool billing clarity.

Proposed technical approach (what we'll propose to them in the deep-dive):
- Dedicated reserved pool: 4x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs in their region (us-west) + 4x burst GPUs that can be pre-warmed on demand. This gives isolation and predictable baseline cost.
- Isolation layer: logical tenancy at runtime + per-tenant KMS integration for model artifact encryption; if they require absolute network separation we present Private (VPC) deployment as option.
- Latency: with prefix KV caching and fine-tuned batching config we can hit P95 <=150ms; P99 will be model-dependent — expect 200–320ms for some 70B workloads at peak; we should capture a small eval prompt set during the deep-dive to size accurately.

Commercial ask for Marissa: draft a pricing option with 3 alternatives — 4-GPU reserve, 6-GPU reserve, 4 + 4 (baseline + burst) with annual and monthly commit lines. Include a clear line-item for burst billing and network egress.

Dylan: please schedule the deep-dive with Alyssa/Nate for next Tue/Thu afternoon PT slots. In that meeting we need to confirm: network path (peering or Private), KMS integration (which provider), and run the quick eval prompts. Bring a SRE on our side if possible.

Vivek: prepare a short runbook paragraph on isolation options and a list of logs/artifacts we can provide for SOC2 answers. Target: draft by EOD Tue.

I will aggregate answers to their SOC2 PDF once they confirm any missing fields.

Hannah
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hannah / team — thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick items:

1) NDA / procurement kickoff: we'd like to get an NDA in place so our security team can share a slightly larger questionnaire. Can you send a DocuSign link?
2) Deep-dive timing: Tue 11/24 14:00 PT works for both of us. Please confirm and add a calendar invite.
3) On sizing: the 4+4 model sounds reasonable as a starting point. We'd want an explicit definition of "burst" (how many minutes of pre-warm, billing granularity).
